item.title: ‘Could be something good’: NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule strikes softer tone on delimitation Bill
item.description: NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule struck a softer tone on the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, saying her party would examine its provisions and support it if it served the country's interests. She said opposing every government proposal was not necessary. Sule also dismissed speculation about her party joining the NDA or her getting a ministerial berth as "gossip".

item.title: A commitment to strengthen our Constitution
item.description: On Constitution Day, the Prime Minister underscores the pivotal role of the Constitution in shaping Indian democracy and society. He elaborates on various steps taken toward fostering social justice, economic parity, and inclusivity through government initiatives. The article reflects on key amendments enhancing constitutional rights and their benefits for marginalized groups, while also tackling historical governance issues.
item.dc:creator: Prime Minister Narendra Modi

item.title: Chemistry most popular subject after English for 12th CBSE students
item.description: In 2027, the CBSE has achieved an impressive milestone with 19 lakh candidates registering for Class 12. An encouraging trend reveals a marked rise in science registrations, notably in chemistry, physics, and mathematics. Notably, the disparity between chemistry and business studies has skyrocketed since 2019. This surge aligns with a national educational shift, showcasing a clear preference for science over commerce fields.
item.dc:creator: Manash Pratim Gohain

item.title: 7th high court posting? Justice Rao may be Karnataka Chief Justice
item.description: Justice M S Ramachandra Rao has been recommended for the position of Chief Justice of the Karnataka high court. This potential appointment would mark his seventh high court assignment since 2012 when he became a judge. He has previously served as Chief Justice in four high courts over a short period. Justice Rao has experienced multiple transfers throughout his judicial career due to various circumstances.
item.dc:creator: Dhananjay Mahapatra

item.title: ‘Fighting against BJP or us?’ Congress slams Samajwadi Party over its list
item.description: Congress MP Imran Masood expressed doubts about the intentions of Samajwadi Party during ongoing seat-sharing negotiations. The discussions, which lasted 3.5 hours, were complicated by SP's announcement of five candidates, causing tension. Masood emphasized that Congress seeks a significant number of seats for the 2027 elections while supporting Akhilesh Yadav for CM. SP leaders dismissed Masood's concerns as personal and affirmed no formal objections were raised.
item.dc:creator: Pervez Iqbal Siddiqui, Shailvee Sharda, Sandeep Rai

item.title: Lamp not lit atop deepathoon, Supreme Court to hear contempt case
item.description: The Tamil Nadu government has not complied with the Supreme Court's order regarding the Karthigai Deepam lamp lighting. This non-compliance may trigger contempt proceedings against the Madurai Collector, despite his apology. Various political parties and the Madurai district administration oppose the lighting of the lamp atop the deepathoon. The Collector reported efforts to follow the Supreme Court's directive, which were ultimately unsuccessful.
item.dc:creator: Amit Anand Choudhary

item.title: India tops in videos removed from YouTube
item.description: YouTube took down approximately 34.4 lakh videos from India in the second quarter of 2026. This number represented a 28% increase from the previous quarter's removals. Globally, child safety issues were responsible for the majority of video removals. Additionally, Indian courts and government agencies sent numerous removal requests to Google. Police primarily initiated these requests, reflecting a growing trend in content regulation.

item.title: Trump slaps new tariffs on 14 nations; India faces additional 17%
item.description: Rejecting claims of surplus capacity in any sector, the Indian government emphasises its commitment to forging a strong bilateral trade agreement with the US. Recent tariff negotiations hit a snag following a US Supreme Court ruling, temporarily halting progress. However, prior to this, an accord on extra tariffs was already negotiated. Optimism remains high among Indian officials that the deal can be finalised, contingent on the US's tariff policy developments.

item.title: ‘Our artists bringing new perspectives to art world’: PM Modi after Venice Biennale award
item.description: The India Pavilion received the Visitors’ Lion Award for Best National Participation at the Venice Art Biennale. Curated by Amin Jaffer, it featured five contemporary artists exploring themes of memory and migration. Prime Minister Narendra Modi acknowledged this achievement as a significant moment for India’s cultural landscape. The pavilion returned to Biennale Arte after a seven-year gap, showcasing diverse Indian perspectives and heritage.

item.title: Meta officials meet Congress over suspended accounts
item.description: In New Delhi, Meta representatives held discussions with Congress social media officials amid growing complaints about account suspensions and content deletions affecting the opposition. Supriya Shrinate raised critical concerns about what she deemed interference by Meta in political issues. In response, the officials clarified that they strictly comply with Indian content laws and maintain their stance of political impartiality throughout these processes.

item.title: Delhi to Dhaka: Probe minority attacks, Hasina passport a separate issue
item.description: In response to escalating violence against minorities in Bangladesh, India has expressed its serious concerns, urging the government there to conduct an extensive investigation. The Ministry of External Affairs noted the unique circumstances surrounding Sheikh Hasina's passport and extradition request, highlighting that these matters are being processed according to established protocols. Furthermore, two Indian nationals suffered injuries in a recent Houthi assault in Riyadh, prompting a strong condemnation from India.

item.title: Bail to be granted under UAPA when there is delay in trial, says Supreme Court
item.description: The Supreme Court has confirmed that its authority to grant bail cannot be overridden by stringent laws. It ruled in favor of a government doctor who has been jailed for over four years. Additionally, the Court granted bail to senior officials involved in a significant corruption case in Rajasthan. These decisions highlight ongoing tensions in bail jurisprudence amid contradictory orders from different benches.
item.dc:creator: Amit Anand Choudhary

item.title: Exporters in better position but brace for uncertainty
item.description: Indian exporters are adapting to potential tariffs from the United States while they finalize a trade agreement. The impact of these tariffs may create temporary uncertainty for exporters as they manage future orders. Current strategies involve rushing shipments to avoid increased costs before the new tariffs kick in. Exporters believe that negotiating a reduced tariff rate will provide a competitive advantage in the market.
item.dc:creator: Sidhartha

item.title: Election Commission: Rectify wrong roll entries during SSR via Form
item.description: Form 8 is being used for rectifying inaccuracies in the electoral roll during the special summary revision. Booth-level officers will verify mismatched entries to ensure accurate voter information collection. Electors can flag incorrect details, and booth-level officers must confirm these. Changes to demographic particulars must be authorized and verified by the competent authority after proper application. The electoral registration officer will manage the processing of applications according to the regulations.
item.dc:creator: Bharti Jain

item.title: Cabinet ministers advised to avoid foreign travel; Parliament session likely by December 15
item.description: Cabinet ministers have been advised to avoid international travel as Parliament may be convened before mid-December. The government aims to introduce a Constitution amendment bill for women's reservation during the next session. This proposal, linked with delimitation, could expand Lok Sabha's strength significantly. Opposition parties have raised concerns regarding its implications, particularly for state representation.
item.dc:creator: Dipak K Dash and Kumar Rakesh

item.title: After 30 years in jail, former Punjab CM Beant Singh's assassin seeks parity with Rajiv Gandhi's killer in SC
item.description: Balwant Singh Rajoana, who has been incarcerated for over three decades, is seeking mercy to have his death sentence reduced. His appeal references the recent release of AG Perarivalan, a former death row inmate turned lawyer. Senior counsel Mukul Rohatgi stresses Rajoana's transformation during imprisonment, while the Centre, represented by ASG KM Nataraj, counters that Rajoana's historical anti-constitutional statements warrant denial.
item.dc:creator: Amit Anand Choudhary

item.title: Missing businessman's non-bailable warrant cancelled in AJL case, ED to move high court
item.description: A special MP/MLA court in Rouse Avenue cancelled a non-bailable warrant against businessman Dinesh Pandey. The Enforcement Directorate is surprised and plans to appeal this decision in the Delhi high court. Pandey is reportedly involved in transferring Rs 10.4 crore through a shell company to Associated Journals Ltd. The court criticized the investigating officer for using a sealed cover, which is typically standard practice.
item.dc:creator: Pradeep Thakur
